sections.name: DomainErrorCode, STATUS
sections.title: Error codes and status map
sections.what: Lists the allowed error reasons, such as not found, forbidden or rate limited, and the web status each one becomes.
sections.why: Keeps the mapping from problem to web response in one place.

sections.name: DomainError, isDomainError
sections.title: Domain error class
sections.what: The error object services throw. It stores the code and looks up its status, and a helper lets handlers recognise it.
sections.why: Likely reason: handlers can tell expected problems apart from crashes.
sections.watch_out: Errors from other libraries are not domain errors, so handlers still need a fallback.

summary: Defines the one error type that services throw and how each error maps to a web status code.
purpose: Lets the service layer report problems such as not found or invalid input in one consistent way.
why: The file comment says route handlers turn these errors into HTTP statuses, so services do not need to know about web responses.
how: Lists the allowed error codes, maps each to a status number, and creates a DomainError that carries the code and status. A helper checks whether an error is one of these.
inputs: An error code and a message.
outputs: An error object with code, message and status.
risks: A new code added to the list must get a status here; the map is typed, so the compiler should catch a missing one.
debug: If a request returns an odd status, check the code the service threw and this map.
